Subject: Clarify EU residency adder + baseline hosted rates

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — Novalytics is evaluating Redwood for two production use cases (customer support generation and a small analytics assistant). Before we loop legal, procurement needs a clear view of your hosted rate card and how regional surcharges / data residency adders are applied. A few specific asks: 

- Can you share the current baseline hosted API price per 1k tokens for the Standard generation profile?
- How do you apply EU data-residency adders (flat fee vs % uplift)? Do you have a published matrix for region tiers (EU / APAC / other)?
- For a committed 12-month term at expected volumes (~2M tokens/month), what discount tiers do you offer and do residency adders reduce with committed capacity?
- Any SLA implications (SLO, uptime) when we select EU residency vs default US hosting?

Appreciate a concise breakdown we can insert into our procurement packet. If there's an updated rate card or example SOW you can attach that would accelerate review.

Looking to get this to our CFO and legal by end of next week.

Thanks,

Novalytics, Inc.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify EU residency adder + baseline hosted rates

Hi Lucia — great to hear from you and glad the demo was helpful. Attaching our latest rate card which includes example pricing paths and residency adders. High level notes below (short summary for procurement):

- Baseline (hosted API, Standard generation): $0.030 per 1k tokens (generation + prompt combined).
- EU residency adder: typically a percentage uplift applied to the baseline; standard published tier is 12-18% depending on region and required controls. On the attached rate card we call this out as a % uplift and show equivalent $/1k examples.
- Residency charging model: we support two flavors — (1) zone-hosted option (data stored/served in EU region) which is a % uplift, or (2) a dedicated-hosted profile (reserved capacity / Dedicated) that can be priced as a flat premium for predictable throughput.
- Commit discounts: we offer stepped committed-volume discounts (monthly commit bands at 6mo/12mo). For a 12-month commit at ~2M tokens/mo we can move to the mid-tier discount (example: 15% off baseline) — that discount applies before residency uplift. In practice the residency uplift is applied to the net price unless you select Dedicated capacity, where we can negotiate an integrated quote.
- SLA: EU zone-hosted (hosted API, residency adders) retains the standard Redwood SLA for hosted customers. If you require a stricter SLA (higher uptime, faster failover, dedicated capacity), we recommend Dedicated or Private which are contractually available and priced separately.

Attached: Redwood-Hosted-Rate-Card-v2.pdf (includes sample math for 500k/2M/10M token profiles).

Proposed next step: quick 30-min pricing touch with Rohan (copied) to run a worked example for your 2M token scenario and flush out SOW requirements. I can also share a template SOW if legal needs something to review.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Lucia — thanks for the specific asks. Below is a compact worked example and answers to the transfer/SOW questions. If this looks right I can get a clean SOW and an updated HubSpot quote to you by tomorrow.

Worked example (2,000,000 tokens/month, Standard generation):
- Baseline: $0.030 per 1k tokens -> monthly base cost = (2,000,000 / 1,000) * $0.030 = $60.00 per month (note: numbers in rate card are per 1k prompt+gen tokens; this is illustrative).
- 12-month commit discount: 15% off baseline -> discounted rate = $0.030 * 0.85 = $0.0255 per 1k -> monthly = (2,000k/1k) * $0.0255 = $51.00/month.
- EU residency uplift (14% example): uplift applied to net price -> final per 1k = $0.0255 * 1.14 = $0.02907 per 1k -> monthly = $58.14.

Key notes:
- Residency uplift is applied after any commit discounts in our hosted pricing model. If you purchase Dedicated/reserved capacity we typically produce an integrated quote where the uplift is baked into the reserved price and can be reduced (we can negotiate the uplift down to single digits with a 12mo commit for high throughput).
- Cross-region transfer: for hosted (zone-hosted) there is no separate per-request cross-region transfer charge for traffic remaining inside the Redwood-hosted region. If you configure clients in different regions that fetch data across regions, your cloud egress costs may apply; Redwood does not currently pass-through third-party cloud egress but we can clearly document expected flows.
- SOW and legal: attaching a short template SOW and marking sections where our standard data residency language and indemnities live. We can accept minor redlines; anything material will need to go through our legal team (Marissa is copied and can shepherd).

Attachments / next steps:
- I'll upload a tailored SOW with the numbers above and a HubSpot quote (link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890).
- If Novalytics is comfortable, we can provision a 30-day pilot with EU residency enabled to validate latency and cost metrics before a 12mo commit.
